Definition: from G2806; a twig or bough (as if broken off):--branch.
KeyPassages: Matthew 13:32; Matthew 21:8; Matthew 24:32; Mark 4:32; Luke 13:19; Romans 11:16
BiblicalUsage: Klados is a branch, a twig broken off. Matthew 13:32 and Mark 4:32 and Luke 13:19 all tell the mustard seed growing into a tree, so that the birds lodge in the branches, Matthew 21:8 has the multitude cutting down branches to straw in the way before Jesus, Matthew 24:32 teaches the parable of the fig tree, when his branch is yet tender and putteth forth leaves, and Romans 11:16 says, if the root be holy, so are the branches.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a branch lives only because it is joined to the root, and it bears only what the root supplies. I hold that the branches cut for the road and the branches of the mustard tree are the same picture, that the kingdom grows where no one expects and shelters whom no one expects.
RelatedTopics: Kingdom of God; Faith; Vine and Branches
